# `Scanner/NullTissue-v0` · Null each marked material with inversion recovery

**A · Signal and contrast** · sequences and steady states · kind 2, set · isolates A9: Inversion recovery: the signed signal and its null point (STIR, FLAIR). [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 92 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 3 % (95 % bounds)

What FLAIR does to fluid and STIR does to fat. The inversion time that nulls a material depends on its T1, on the repetition time (recovery is incomplete when the next inversion arrives) and on how complete the inversion is, so it cannot be looked up: it has to be measured on this object and this system.

```python
import mrgym
env = mrgym.make("Scanner/NullTissue-v0", level=2, seed=0)
obs, info = env.reset()
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A test object with vials of hidden materials; the scanner; a scan-time budget for probing | For each marked region, the inversion time that nulls it in an inversion-recovery scan with a given repetition time | Noise-free scans of the target protocol on the hidden object: every marked region must be nulled by its inversion time |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (a disc of gel with vials), 1.5 T
- Sequences that matter here: ir, se, spgr
- Formulas the agent is given: S(TI) = a - b exp(-TI / T1) at a fixed repetition time; the sign of the signal is in the phase image

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| T1, T2 and proton density of every material | the target scan and its repetition time |
| inversion efficiency | the regions |
| transmit gain and B1 pattern | the pass threshold |
| noise level | the instrument datasheet |
| the 128-bit world seed | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |

## Levels

| Level | Covered by the claim | Hidden-world prior | Budget (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | no: practice level | practice: the world of level 1 with the procedure stated and the first probe already acquired | 185 |
| 1 | yes | long repetition time: the textbook rule TI = ln 2 x T1 is nearly right, once T1 is measured | 150 |
| 2 | yes | repetition time comparable to T1: the null moves with the repetition time | 200 |
| 3 | yes | as level 2 with an incomplete inversion, a miscalibrated transmitter and more noise | 200 |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'ti_ms': {'<region id>': '<milliseconds>'}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts the target scan with the delivered inversion time
- Error: `largest over the regions of: signal in the target scan / signal without the inversion pulse (noise-free)`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for every region, error <= 5 %

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

Run 2026-11-25 on engine `mrgym-engine-0.2.0`, package 0.1.0.dev0: `mrgym gate Scanner/NullTissue-v0 --n 300 --write` (split gate, seeds 0..299; recipes tuned on split tune, seeds <set 0..2>:<0..15>). A level is admitted when the lower bound of the reference is at least 90 %, the upper bound of every must-fail policy is at most 10 % and every ablation required at the level loses at least 25 points (lower bound of the paired difference). Bounds are one-sided, 95 %. Cells: passed / instances (rate; bound).

| Policy | Must | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | 284/300 (94.7 %; lower bound 92.0 %) | 298/300 (99.3 %; lower bound 97.9 %) | 295/300 (98.3 %; lower bound 96.5 %) | three signed probes, fit of a - b exp(-TI / T1), transfer to the target repetition time, one check scan |
| `prior` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | no scan; TI = ln 2 x the middle of the plausible T1 range |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | 3/300 (1.0 %; upper bound 2.6 %) | 1/300 (0.3 %; upper bound 1.6 %) | 1/300 (0.3 %; upper bound 1.6 %) | one token scan, then one constant inversion time tuned on other worlds |
| `brute_force` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 1/300 (0.3 %; upper bound 1.6 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | probes on a fixed grid of inversion times, delivers the one with the smallest signal |
| `wrong_units` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | the reference's inversion time in seconds |
| `textbook` | ablation | 198/300 (66.0 %; 28.7 points below the reference, lower bound 24.3) not required here | 42/300 (14.0 %; 85.3 points below the reference, lower bound 81.9) | 10/300 (3.3 %; 95.0 points below the reference, lower bound 92.7) | measures T1, then TI = ln 2 x T1 (ignores the repetition time and the inversion efficiency) |

Verdict per level: level 1 **admitted**; level 2 **admitted**; level 3 **admitted**.
Blind ceiling (the must-fail policy that passes most often): level 1 `fixed_recipe#2` 1.0 % (upper bound 2.6 %); level 2 `brute_force` 0.3 % (upper bound 1.6 %); level 3 `fixed_recipe#2` 0.3 % (upper bound 1.6 %).
Reference, error of its answer (median / 95th percentile): level 1 0.01386 / 0.05189; level 2 0.0125 / 0.03404; level 3 0.01277 / 0.03433; scan time used (median): level 1 116 s, level 2 176.6 s, level 3 180.4 s.

## Validity

What could change the right answer of this environment. Measured 2026-11-25 on engine `mrgym-engine-0.2.0`: `mrgym validate --perturb Scanner/NullTissue-v0 --level 2 --n 30 --draws 2 --write`. The reference policy `reference` replayed level 2 on 60 instances (validity:0..validity:29) with one piece of physics changed per row, and was scored against the changed world. Unperturbed it passes 60 of 60 (94 to 100 %, 95 % interval).

| Perturbation | Size | Passed | Difference (95 % interval) | Error shift (tolerances) | Answer moved | Class | Handled by |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `rf_fast`: excitation pulse | time-bandwidth 2 instead of the console's | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `rf_sharp`: excitation pulse | time-bandwidth 8 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `rf_hamming`: excitation pulse | Hamming instead of Hann window | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `rf_rect`: excitation pulse | ideal rectangular slice profile (the engine of 0.1.0) | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `ideal_spoiling`: steady state of spgr / afi | ideal spoiling instead of the EPG | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `fat_singlepeak`: fat spectrum | one line at -3.4 ppm instead of six | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `noise_x0.5`: receiver noise | x 0.5 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `noise_x2`: receiver noise | x 2 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `magnitude_only`: what a region read-out returns | no complex mean (magnitude data only) | 0/60 | -100 (-100 to -91) points | - | 0 % | flips | - |
| `tx_gain_x2`: transmit-gain error | x 2 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `b1_strong`: B1+ pattern | amplitude 0.35 to 0.45 (QA phantom) / x 3 (anatomy) | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `b0_x5`: off-resonance field and its through-slice gradient | x 5 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `cf_x5`: centre-frequency error | x 5 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `rx_surface`: receive profile | x exp(-(y - y_top) / 70 mm): a surface coil | 57/60 | -5 (-14 to +2) points | +0.13 | 0 % | noise-like | - |
| `edge_sharp`: soft boundaries of the object | half-width 0.05 mm instead of 0.5 mm | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `edge_soft`: soft boundaries of the object | half-width 2.0 mm | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.02 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `adc_low`: diffusion coefficient | 0.05 um^2/ms in every material (oil-like) | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `relax_shift`: relaxation times | T1 x 1.2, T2 x 0.8 in every material | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.01 | 98 % | flips, the reference follows | - |
| `inv_weak`: inversion efficiency | 0.80 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | -0.03 | 100 % | flips, the reference follows | - |
| `fatsat_weak`: fat-saturation efficiency | 0.75 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `fatsat_off`: centre frequency of the fat-saturation pulse | +60 Hz at 3 T | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `grad_delay_x5`: residual gradient delay (EPI ghost) | x 5 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `gnl`: gradient non-linearity | positions scaled by 1 - 0.03 (r / 250 mm)^2 | 60/60 | +0 (-6 to +6) points | +0.00 | 0 % | robust | - |
| `motion_ghost`: periodic motion | every line x (1 + 0.1 cos(2 pi 0.25 Hz t)) | 15/60 | -75 (-84 to -61) points | +1.54 | 7 % | flips | - |

Classes: *flips* = the pass rate falls by more than 10 points (interval excluding 0) or the unperturbed deliverable fails on more than 10 % of the perturbed worlds; *robust* = difference at least -5 points with the interval above -10; *noise-like* = neither, and the error moves by less than a quarter of the tolerance; *undecided* = more instances are needed. "The reference follows" = the right answer moves and the reference still passes, because it measures the quantity.

Not run, because the engine does not have the physics: `transient` (needs the approach to steady state in the engine; the engine serves the periodic state); `array8_sos` (needs a receive array with root-sum-of-squares combination; the engine has one channel); `spoiler_lobe` (needs the b-factor of a spoiler lobe instead of a gradient that is constant over TR); `afi_phase_per_pulse` (needs an RF phase counted per pulse in the EPG (the engine counts raster positions)); `fov_free` (a verifier-side row of the NoWrap family (optimum with free centre and rotation); not a physics perturbation).

Cannot be tested here at all (not modelled, no emulation): magnetisation transfer and exchange; restricted or anisotropic diffusion; flow, perfusion and physiological motion beyond one periodic line-modulation model; eddy currents, concomitant fields, gradient impulse response; SAR in W/kg, local SAR, nerve stimulation; B0 drift and heating; anything through the slice beyond independent columns: slice positioning, multi-slice cross-talk, slab wrap of the 3D mode; parallel transmit; vendor pulses, filters and distortion correction; coil loading and receive arrays.

No row is a comparison with a scanner: MR Gym has never been compared with data from one.

# Null each marked material with inversion recovery
A test object with vials of unknown materials lies in the field of
view. For each marked region the examination needs an inversion-recovery image in which the material of that region
gives no signal. The scan is the same for all of them except for its inversion time:
    sequence ir, tr_ms 2160, te_ms at the console minimum, matrix 128, bandwidth_hz_per_px 300,
    field of view at the console default, 1 average, slice 5 mm.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre; each lies inside one homogeneous material):
  R1: y 12.74, x 57.56, radius 11.5
  R2: y -13.77, x -51.91, radius 11.5
  R3: y 52.66, x -13.63, radius 11.5
Deliver one inversion time per region (R1, R2, R3) with `submit`. The target scans are not run in this episode: the scanner
evaluates the inversion times you deliver. Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names. That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
Nothing about the materials or the state of the system is known in advance.

Passing: for every region, in the target scan with the inversion time you delivered for it, its signal is at most
5 % of its signal in the same scan without the inversion pulse. The scanner's log must show that you
measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 200 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 48 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's scan is noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
